title: Test day six
hook: notice what's missing: why does Genesis say God finished on the seventh day, the day of rest?
tomorrow: how many times should you think something over?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: loved. The part of the rule you'd replay, the weight that pulls the rest. Today, the opposite of a part: the gap.

A to-do app will happily show you every box you checked today. It has no box for what isn't on the list. Here's an odd line near the start of the Bible. God makes the world, day by day, and by the end of the sixth day it's all there. Then Genesis says, in the King James Version: "And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made." On the seventh day? Nothing was made on the seventh day. So what was still missing?
screen: `A LIST OF EVERYTHING YOU DID.` → `IT'S ALL MADE BY DAY SIX.` → `ENDED ON THE SEVENTH?`

segments.voice: The rabbis noticed it too. In Genesis Rabbah, an early collection of their readings, and later in Rashi, the medieval commentator, the answer comes as a riddle. What did the world lack? Rest. When the Sabbath came, rest came, and then the work was finished. So rest isn't the empty space after creation. In this reading it's the last thing created. The next verse goes further: "And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it." Abraham Joshua Heschel, a modern rabbi, pointed out that the first thing the Bible calls holy is not a mountain or an altar but a day. That's the teaching behind Shabbat. Shabbat runs from Friday sunset to Saturday nightfall, kept with candles, blessings, a long meal, and a rest from work. Not a break from the week. The week's finish. Something to pass on tonight: by this reading, a world with everything in it was still unfinished, because nothing in it was resting. So on day six of a test, look for what's missing. Some gaps are flaws. Some are the very thing that would finish it. If your rule is all doing, the rabbis' riddle asks a fair question: where's the seventh day?
screen: `WHAT DID THE WORLD LACK? REST.` · `THE LAST THING CREATED.` · `GOD BLESSED THE SEVENTH DAY.` · `SHABBAT: THE WEEK'S FINISH.` · then, large: `SOME GAPS ARE THE FINISH.`

segments.voice: For this sit, do nothing that counts as doing: hands open, no planning, no fixing. Call it a seventh-day minute. Near the end, let one question rise on its own: what is my rule missing?
Test day six: the day you notice what your rule is missing. In the rabbis' riddle, the world was missing rest.
Keep this one: missing, and sometimes the gap is what finishes the work. See you tomorrow.
